sam: Heads-up — overnight perf sweep on the mixed farm flagged weird KV cache behavior on SM92 nodes. latency p50 for small chat workloads jumped ~18% vs baseline. :eyeglasses:

mara: Ugh. Any obvious kernel misroute?

sam: Logs show fastpath kernel chosen but KV hit rate is low. snippet from runtime probe: 
```
hw_sig: SM92; driver: 537.23; tensor_cores: reported=true; bf16_ok=false; kernel_path=fast_kc1
kv_stats: hits=42%, lookups=120k, cache_evictions=18k
batch_stats: avg_batch=1.8, seq_med=128
```

jing: BF16 flagged false on SM92? that seems off — SM92 should do bf16 on tensor cores. driver 537.23 rings a bell. did we run the capprobe change last week?

sam: We did. The probe now uses a microbench MP test that prefers bf16 only if tc_fp32_roundtrip < 1.2x fp32. On some machines the microbench returns noisy results and clears the bf16 flag. That makes runtime pick the fp32-compatible kernel even when a bf16 kernel would be faster — causing KV pathways to be suboptimal.

mara: Can you paste the microbench output from one SM92 box?

sam: Sure: 
```
microbench tc_fp32_roundtrip=1.27; memcpy=0.78ms; small_gemm_throughput=45.2 TFLOPS; flags: bf16_detected=false
```

perf-bot: nightly-bench summary: sm92-smallchat: p50 24.3ms (baseline 20.6ms), p95 86ms (baseline 70ms). kernel mix: 65% fast_kc1, 30% safe_kc2, 5% fallback_fp32. KV cache heatmaps show cold-starts concentrated on nodes where bf16_detected=false.

jing: Sounds like probe noise on short microbench. I remember driver 537 has a known scheduling jitter on CUDA kernel timers that skews sub-ms numbers. We saw similar with sm86 earlier.

mara: Two quick mitigation options: 1) make capprobe use a longer microbench (5s) and median reduce, or 2) add hysteresis for kernel selection: only flip bf16-eligible flag if probe is stable across N boots or N probes. Which has lower risk?

sam: Hysteresis is safer and faster to roll. We also need a runtime fallback to prefer BF16 kernel if seqlen and batch look right (seq <= 128 and avg_batch>=1.5) even if probe is negative. That could recover perf while we stabilize probing.

jing: Agree. Proposed change: 
- capprobe: require 3/5 positive microbench samples OR driver >= 538 to mark bf16_ok=true
- runtime kernel heuristic: if bf16_ok=false but (seq_median<=128 && avg_batch>=1.5 && kv_hit_rate>30%) then prefer bf16_fastpath with a guarded guardrail: limit to 10% of traffic initially (canary).

mara: Also let's raise KV warmup TTL from 60s -> 180s on these nodes to reduce eviction churn until we confirm behavior.

sam: I'll draft a canary rollout plan for the heuristic and attach a quick toggle: `runtime.autotune.prefer_bf16_canary_pct` (default 0).

deploy-bot: deploy plan created: PR #4782, canary tag=sm92-bf16-autotune-canary, route 10% traffic to canary, duration 24h, rollback on p95 increase > 10% or error-rate spike. :shipit:

mara: Nice. One more check: add a perf counter that tracks "probe_flip_rate" (how often hw flags change per week) so we can detect noisy machines and blacklist them from auto-flips.

sam: Will add that. Action items: 
- sam: implement runtime heuristic + config toggle + KV TTL bump (ETA today)
- jing: update capprobe sampling and add driver whitelist check (ETA tomorrow)
- mara: monitor canary + add probe_flip_rate dashboard (ETA EOD)

jing: If we push canary quickly, I'll watch for regressions on the 3 problematic hosts I already flagged. :eyes:

sam: Thanks — starting the PR now.

mara: Thanks team. Follow-up: if canary looks good, we should bake the heuristic into the default autotune profile but keep a conservative threshold for sequences >256.

sam: Agreed.

perf-bot: NOTE: saved raw bench logs to s3://redwood-perf/2026-05/1798765432-sm92-sweep.tar.gz

mara: Perfect, will dig through the logs after lunch. :coffee:
